intro: In the middle of the Safranbolu market, in Karabük province, stands Cinci Han, a caravanserai from 1645. This two-storey Ottoman han kept animals below and merchants above — and today it is in use as a hotel.
history: The han was built in 1645 for Cinci Hoca, a powerful judge of the day. Its plan is simple and practical: animals and stores below, merchants' rooms above. Safranbolu's place on the Silk Road kept it working for centuries, and today it is in use as a hotel.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the courtyard and the upper-floor rooms. Look into the stables, and take a moment with the stone façade.
facts: Did you know? Cinci Hoca owed his fortune to his influence at court, and he was executed not long after the han was finished. Built in 1645, the han kept working for centuries thanks to Safranbolu's place on the Silk Road.
outro: This brings our journey through Cinci Han to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These stones have waited for centuries; let them keep waiting for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
